searchText: Has there been any thought about requiring miners supply a bond with their block that is burned if their block is invalid (not properly constructed)? Any miner could include such a block in a valid block (like uncles) and receive some small reward. The idea here is to make it so that nodes can lazily validate blocks without having to worry about DoS vectors. You would only validate that the miner signature is valid, and the miner has funds to cover the bond, then you would forward the block. If the bond is say, 3 ETH, that means a *single* invalid block propogated across the network would cost the "miner" 3 ETH. (hand waving a bit around how the miners lock up capital for this bond so they can't move it out of the way after the DoS attack) This *could* improve block propagation time across the network (because blocks propagate much faster), which would lead to lower uncle rates and can be beneficial as block size rises. Note: This would help blocks propagate faster across the network, but it would not help miners who need to fully execute parent block before they can build next-block. <jadler> This already exists. It's called Proof-of-Work. See Section 4 of the Bitcoin design paper: https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf (re @eth1x_bridge_bot: <Micah> The idea here is to make it so that nodes can lazily validate blocks without having to worry about DoS vectors.) <vbuterin> yeah, I think the block reward opportunity cost is already incentive enough to discourage publishing bad blocks Do clients currently propogate blocks as soon as they validate the work, but before they validate the block? <vbuterin> Yes <vbuterin> That's been happening for a while now <vbuterin> And properly implementing that was responsible for the uncle rate decrease from ~25% to ~8% in 2018-19, as I recall Awesome, ignore the above. You are right <@713071416521785444> that PoW achieves the same goal in a simpler way! <jadler> https://github.com/openethereum/openethereum/issues/9576
